chunks: And my father, 'Ali ibn al-Husayn, and a group of my scholars narrated to me from Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Muhammad ibn Khald, from al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather al-Husayn ibn Rashid, from Yunus ibn 'Abdi, who said:

Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Whoever visits al-Husayn (peace be upon him) on the night of the fifteenth of Sha'ban, and the night of al-Fitr, and the night of 'Arafah, in one year, Allah will record for him one thousand purified Hajj and one thousand accepted 'Umrah, and a thousand needs of this life and the Hereafter will be fulfilled for him.

key_terms.حَوَائِجِ الدُّنْيَا وَالْآخِرَةِ: needs of this world and the Hereafter
key_terms.شَعْبَانَ: Sha'ban (the eighth month of the Islamic calendar)

ai.seo_question: What are the rewards for visiting Imam Husayn on the 15th of Sha'ban, Eid al-Fitr, and Night of Arafah?
ai.summary: In Kamil al-Ziyarat, Ibn Qulawayh records this tradition linking the visitation of Imam al-Husayn (a.s.) to the celestial nights of the 15th of Sha'ban (Laylat al-Bara'at), Eid al-Fitr, and 'Arafah, highlighting the interconnection between the Ahl al-Bayt and key moments in the Islamic calendar. This accumulation of rewards within a single year signifies a comprehensive purification of the soul, merging the commemoration of the Prophet's fasting and Eid with the pivotal day of standing before God at 'Arafah. The promise of a thousand accepted Hajj and 'Umrah underscores the immense spiritual weight of these visits in Shia devotional practice.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 7. My father, ‘Ali ibn Ḥusain and all of my scholars narrated to me from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillāh, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ‘Isā, from Muḥammad ibn Khālid, from Qāsim ibn Yaḥyā, from his grandfather Ḥasan ibn Rāshid, from Yūnus ibn Żabyān, who said:

Abū ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) said: Allāh will register one thousand purified Hajj and one thousand accepted ‘Umrah and will grant one thousand requests pertaining to this life and the Hereafter for those who go to the Ziyārah of Ḥusain (a.s.) on the night of the fifteenth of Sha’bān, on the night of Fiťr, and on the night of ‘Arafah all in the same year.
